summary: Draft covers the durability decomposition, TAC, App Store, DMA, multiple decomposition, both reader priors, supply chain and silicon well. Eight corpus clusters present in the vault are missing or thinly used: DOJ v. Apple claim breadth (lock-in itself, not just NFC), court-surfaced App Store profitability (78% operating margin, Epic trial), the CEO-transition cluster (8 notes reduced to two sentences), Apple Pay never sized, the affirmative iOS-27 supercycle case, the named live sell-side bear case (Jefferies), the TSMC 20-F primary filing behind the Taiwan claim, and the crowding/equity-duration paper clusters. Body is 65KB before Sources, at the upper end of the norm, with 8.1-8.4 restating the Kurzantwort.

findings.location: Abschnitt 4.4 (EU DMA und US v. Apple), plus qualifier in 7.1 and 8.2
findings.issue: DOJ v. Apple is reduced to NFC/Apple-Pay hardware access. The corpus shows the case's theory of harm is ecosystem lock-in itself: the DOJ's two high-level practices are (1) App Store rules that increase reliance on Apple hardware and (2) deliberate limits on cross-platform functionality (super apps, cloud-streaming apps, cross-platform messaging, smartwatch interoperability, digital wallets) designed to raise switching costs. That is precisely the mechanism the draft's own bull case in 7.1 and 8.2 leans on ('Der Lock-in ist strukturell fuer die zyklische Klasse und ein echtes Bull-Argument'). The research_query asks which earnings hang on arrangements a court can void; a live US case whose remedy would void the switching-cost architecture is the largest unpriced item in the report and is never characterised at that level. The vault also shows the plaintiff coalition widened (four additional states joined), which bears on the durability of the case.
findings.evidence: Unused notes: doj-v-apple-monopolization-of-the-smartphone-aaf (AAF primer, 28 Mar 2024: 'The DOJ cites two high-level practices ... 1) enforcing unfair App Store rules designed to increase reliance on Apple's hardware, and 2) limiting cross-platform functionality of applications and devices to prevent current users from switching'); office-of-public-affairs-four-additional-states-join-justice-departments-suit-ag. The cited note judge-allows-justice-departments-iphone-monopolization-suit-to-proceed-mintz [54] is used only for market shares and the NFC claim.
findings.recommendation: In 4.4, extend the DOJ paragraph by two or three sentences: name the two alleged practices and the conduct categories (super apps, cloud gaming, cross-platform messaging, smartwatches, wallets), note the widened state-AG coalition, and state explicitly that a DOJ remedy would act on the switching-cost layer rather than on a revenue line, which is why it cannot be sized in Bruttogewinn-Prozent but is not therefore small. Then add one clause to the Festlegung in 7.1 conceding that the structural-lock-in bull argument is itself a defendant in an open US case, and one clause to 8.2 so the bull rebuttal does not rest on a lock-in the draft elsewhere lists as legally contested.

findings.location: Abschnitt 1.2 (App-Store-Kommissionen: nur Anbieterschaetzungen) and the Vorbehalt auf Ergebnisebene in 1.4
findings.issue: The draft asserts 'Hier existiert keine Gerichts- oder Gutachterzahl' for App Store margin and that higher circulating values are 'weder gerichtlich festgestellt noch Bruttomargen'. The vault contains exactly such a Gutachterzahl: Epic's expert witness Ned Barnes put the App Store's operating margin at 78% for FY2019 (75% for FY2018), entered in the Epic v. Apple trial record and reported via Bloomberg. It is an adversarial expert estimate rather than a court finding, but it is an operating margin, i.e. the quantity the draft's OI-Basis row needs, and the draft instead builds that row from a uniform 68.5% OI/Bruttogewinn ratio plus the unsourced assumption that opex attaches to the non-exposed classes. Under the run's deep-inference directive that derived claim should name the sourced claims it rests on, and here an independent court-surfaced anchor exists and is ignored.
findings.evidence: Unused note apple-runs-app-store-with-78-profit-margin-according-to-court-testimony-9to5mac: 'the App Store ran at a 78% profit margin in 2019 ... from a court testimony from an Epic Games expert witness Ned Barnes. The profit margin rose from 75% in 2018 to 78% in 2019.' Also unused: united-states-district-court-4 (Rule 52 Order After Trial, Doc. 812) and full-findings-of-the-court-in-epic-games-v-apple-pdf-ios-computing.
findings.recommendation: Correct the audited-absence claim in 1.2: no Apple disclosure and no court FINDING exists, but an adversarial expert estimate from the Epic trial record does (78% operating margin FY2019, 75% FY2018, Barnes for Epic), used only as a corroborating upper anchor given its provenance (Epic-retained, 2019 vintage, operating not gross). Then add one sentence to the Vorbehalt in 1.4 noting that this figure independently supports the opex-allocation assumption currently asserted as merely 'plausibel'.

findings.issue: An eight-note corpus cluster on the Cook-to-Ternus CEO transition is collapsed into two sentences of deliberate abstention ('Die CEO-Uebergabe zum 1. September 2026 enthielt keine Strategieaussage; aus Ternus' Hardware-Laufbahn wird hier nichts abgeleitet'). The abstention is defensible as ORIGIN evidence for Leserannahme I, but the corpus carries a different, forward-looking fact: Ternus has explicitly re-centred strategy on the iPhone as the AI-era hub, in deliberate contrast to Cook's decade of arguing Apple is more than the iPhone. Over a 2-5 year holding horizon that is a first-order governance fact - a management change plus a stated reorientation toward the very hardware class the draft argues is over-multiplied. Section 8.6 already makes the 'intelligent personal hub' wager its closing image but sources it to one keynote quote, with no execution- or key-person-risk treatment.
findings.evidence: Cluster tags: ceo-transition (6), john-ternus (6), apple-governance (6). Only [61] apple-ceo-john-ternus-says-the-best-ai-device-is-still-the-iphone-techcrunch and [62] john-ternus-is-now-apples-ceo-macrumors are cited. Unused: apples-new-ceo-is-reviving-a-steve-jobs-strategy-from-25-years-ago-techcrunch ('This contrasts with the approach taken by former CEO Tim Cook, who tried time and again to convince Wall Street that Apple was more than just the iPhone'), ft-apple-intensifies-succession-planning-as-cooks-exit-looms, apple-ceo-tim-cook-is-stepping-down-john-ternus-set-to-replace-him-abc-news, tim-cook-steps-down-as-apple-ceo-tomorrow-macrumors, tim-cook-comments-on-his-final-day-as-apple-ceo-macrumors, apple-ceo-tim-cook-stepping-down-john-ternus-taking-over-macrumors, everything-apple-announced-at-its-fall-iphone-event-from-the-foldable-iphone-duo.
findings.recommendation: Keep the abstention in 5.2 but extend it by one sentence distinguishing origin evidence from forward-looking evidence: the transition says nothing about why Apple arrived late, but Ternus's first keynote re-centres strategy on the iPhone in explicit contrast to Cook's 'more than the iPhone' framing, which is a hardware-weighted bet. Then add one clause in 8.6 noting the repositioning is itself new (Sept 2026) and untested, so the 'intelligent personal hub' wager carries first-year-CEO execution risk - an early indicator, not a resolved fact.

findings.location: Abschnitt 6.3 (Richtung: bestaetigt - aber der Taeter ist ein anderer)
findings.issue: Apple Pay is named explicitly in the reader's second prior, yet the report never sizes it - not as a range, not as an audited absence with a stated search. The only treatment is an unsourced inference: 'Apple weist die Apple-Pay-Erloese nicht aus; ihr Interchange-Anteil ist klein relativ zu Services, sodass eine Gebuehrenkompression ohne Netzverdraengung kaum ins Gewicht fiele (Inferenz).' Under the run's deep-inference directive that is a derived claim naming no sourced claim it derives from, and an audited absence asserted without stating what was searched. The corpus supports better: the DMA has already forced NFC opening in the EU, the EC factsheet documents delivered third-party wallet access, and the same complex is a live DOJ count.
findings.evidence: Tag apple-pay carries 6 notes. [18] factsheet-how-the-dma-is-making-smartphones-better-interoperability-and-data-portability and the unused dma-how-the-eus-big-tech-law-changed-citizens-lives-euronews both document EU third-party wallet/NFC access as live; [54] Mintz carries the NFC count. No note in the corpus discloses Apple Pay revenue.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the Apple Pay sentences in 6.3 as a proper audited absence plus a bounded inference: state that no filing, court record or analyst source in the corpus discloses Apple Pay revenue or its interchange share (naming what was searched), that the only anchors are the reported per-transaction interchange share on card volume, and that the report therefore treats Apple Pay as immaterial to the decomposition on an explicitly stated upper bound rather than by assertion. Add that EU NFC opening is already in force and the US equivalent is a DOJ count, so the direction of pressure is documented even where the magnitude is not.

findings.issue: The AI-upgrade-supercycle question (research question 9) is disposed of in two sentences using only replacement-cycle length data, and the strongest version of the supercycle case is never stated before it is dismissed. The brief's non-negotiable is that the reader can argue both cases competently; here the bull case is not argued at all. The corpus carries the mechanism the thesis actually rests on - not sentiment but hardware gating: the advanced Apple Intelligence / agentic-Siri features are gated behind silicon that only a fraction of the ~2.5bn active base owns. Wedbush and JPMorgan are named as holders of the thesis.
findings.evidence: Unused note ios-27-and-the-iphone-upgrade-calculus-why-apples-ai-overhaul-could-unlock-a-new: 'roughly 66% of all active iPhones were running iOS 26 as of February 2026, but the most advanced Apple Intelligence features are gated behind hardware that only a fraction of that base currently owns'; 'Analysts at Wedbush and JPMorgan view this as the ignition switch for a multi-year hardware upgrade supercycle.' The draft's counter-evidence [66][67] is replacement-cycle length, which answers a different claim.
findings.recommendation: Expand the supercycle passage in 5.4 by two or three sentences: state the gating mechanism (advanced features require newer silicon; a large share of the active base is excluded), attribute the thesis (Wedbush, JPMorgan), then adjudicate against it with evidence already in the draft - the 3.84-year plateau, the CIRP finding that first-time buyers do not need the newest model, and 7.2's price-and-mix decomposition. Commit as elsewhere: gating is real but has not bent the cycle in observed data.

findings.issue: The bear case is characterised abstractly while the live, named market bear case sits unused in the corpus: Jefferies downgraded Apple from Hold to Underperform on 10 Aug 2026 with a PT of $263.66 on memory costs plus the cancelled all-glass iPhone, with a rebuttal published the next day. Naming and adjudicating the bear case a reader will actually encounter costs two sentences and serves the brief's success criterion. It also connects to 7.2, where the draft independently establishes memory cost as the binding margin issue - the draft's own evidence partly vindicates the Jefferies leg it never names.
findings.evidence: Unused note opinion-wall-streets-new-apple-bear-case-is-dead-wrong-247-wall-st: 'On August 10, 2026, the firm downgraded Apple from Hold to Underperform with a price target of $263.66, citing rising memory costs and the reported cancellation of the all-glass iPhone.'
findings.recommendation: Add two sentences to 8.3 naming the Jefferies downgrade and adjudicating it: the memory-cost leg is corroborated by the draft's own adjusted-margin work in 7.2 and Parekh's 'more than 100% of that' attribution, while the product-cancellation leg is a single-cycle rumour and not a durability argument. Note that even the sell-side bear case is built on the cyclical class, not the contingent streams - which is the report's point.

findings.location: Abschnitt 7.5 (Lieferkette: Montage schnell, Faehigkeiten langsam, Taiwan binaer)
findings.issue: The Taiwan tail-risk claim - the load-bearing geopolitical finding of the section - rests entirely on [86], a paywalled SemiAnalysis newsletter preview. TSMC's own FY2025 Form 20-F is in the vault and unused. The brief's sourcing instruction weights filings and primary records over commentary; here the opposite happened on the one claim the draft calls binary and unhedgeable.
findings.evidence: Unused note tsm-20251231 (TSMC FY2025 Form 20-F, SEC EDGAR, CIK 0001046179): primary disclosure of fab geography, leading-edge capacity location, the Arizona ramp and the issuer's own geopolitical risk factors. Draft cites only apple-tsmc-the-partnership-that-built-modern-semiconductors [86].
findings.recommendation: Anchor the Taiwan paragraph in 7.5 with one sentence from TSMC's 20-F - leading-edge capacity concentration and overseas-fab ramp schedule as the issuer discloses them - and keep SemiAnalysis for the Apple-specific node-allocation point. This upgrades the evidence tier on a claim the section itself calls binary, without changing the finding.

findings.location: Abschnitt 3.3 (Crowding, Zinsen, Nennerqualitaet) und die Komponententabelle
findings.issue: Two corpus clusters bearing on the two weakest rows of the premium-decomposition table are unused. On crowding, the draft cites only MSCI vendor research plus one contrary JFQA paper and concludes 'nicht bezifferbar'; the vault holds two academic crowding papers with directional findings that permit something sharper - crowding susceptibility is factor-specific (depends on the factor's barriers to entry), and positioning-based crowding measures negatively predict factor returns. On duration, the draft cites Gormsen/Lazarus twice; the implied-equity-duration literature that would place Apple on a duration scale rather than assert 'kurze Cashflow-Duration' is unused. coverage-gaps.md flagged Q5 crowding as the corpus's weakest item, wave 2 filled it, and the draft did not pick the fill up.
findings.evidence: Unused: dynamics-of-factor-crowding-hua-sun-ssrn-5023380 ('crowding susceptibility depends on the factor's barriers'), crowding-and-factor-returns-kang-rouwenhorst-tang-ssrn-3803954 ('crowding measure negatively predicts factor strategy returns'), doi-1011111475-679x12348 (Dechow, Erhard, Sloan & Soliman, implied equity duration), why-is-longhorizon-equity-less-risky-a-durationbased-explanation-of-the-value-pr (Lettau & Wachter, JF 2007), msci-integrated-factor-crowding-model-msci.
findings.recommendation: In 3.3, replace the bare 'Crowding erhoeht damit die Pfadvolatilitaet des Multiples' with one sentence using the academic finding: crowding is factor-specific rather than stock-specific, positioning-based measures predict reversal rather than level, and Apple's quality/low-volatility exposure is therefore a path risk the literature cannot attach to a single name. In the duration row, add the implied-equity-duration citation behind 'kurze Cashflow-Duration' so the claim carries provenance rather than resting on the payout/profitability profile alone.

findings.location: Abschnitte 8.1-8.4, Kurzantwort und die Barrieren-Tabelle in 2.5
findings.issue: Content dilution. The body is 65KB before Sources and Appendix, at the upper end of the reference norm. The verdict chapter is the main source of inflation: the Kurzantwort already states the 19.7-28.3% range, the 'Headline-KGV ist irrefuehrend, aber in anderer Richtung' framing, the 35-38x implicit hardware multiple and the bull-on-existence / bear-on-multiple split. Section 8.1 restates all four in the same order with the same figures; 8.2 and 8.4 then restate the bull rebuttal a second and third time ('Loyalitaet schuetzt die zyklische Klasse, nicht die exponierte' in 8.2 is the same move as 'Die Gewinnbasis ist nicht in Gefahr; ihre Bewertung ist bereits ausgeschoepft' in 8.4, itself already made in the Festlegung of 3.3). Separately, the 2.5 barrier table re-encodes as a table the disclosure-gap and margin-bound material already argued in prose in 1.1 and 1.2.
findings.evidence: Kurzantwort vs 8.1: both open with the 19,7 / 28,3 % range, both assert the headline multiple misleads in the opposite direction to the bear case, both give the 35-38x hardware figure. 3.3 Festlegung ('Die Praemie ist real, aber bereits in Anspruch genommen') vs 8.4 ('Die Gewinnbasis ist nicht in Gefahr; ihre Bewertung ist bereits ausgeschoepft').
findings.recommendation: Tighten three passages rather than cut sections. (1) Reduce 8.1's restatement of the Kurzantwort figures to a single cross-reference sentence and let the table carry the detail. (2) Collapse the overlap between 8.2's bull rebuttal and 8.4's asymmetry paragraph - keep the three-conditions asymmetry in 8.4, delete the repeated 'Loyalitaet schuetzt die zyklische Klasse' formulation from one of the two. (3) Drop the two rows of the 2.5 barrier table that merely repeat 1.1-1.2 prose (disclosure not separate; commission margin without a court value) and keep the rows that add method (opex allocation, legal probabilities, flow/factor share). Recovers roughly 4-6KB without losing a finding.

findings.issue: The opening Kurzantwort and the verdict's 'Was die Evidenz beguenstigt' subsection deliver the same adjudication in near-identical phrasing ('Die Evidenz beguenstigt den Bull-Case bei der Existenz der Ertraege und einen milden Bear-Case beim Multiplikator' vs 'Klar den Bull-Case auf der Existenzebene, leicht den Bear-Case auf der Multiplikatorebene'). The conclusion therefore adds little the reader did not have on page one.
findings.evidence: The Kurzantwort sentence and the bolded opening of 8.4 are the same claim with substituted synonyms; the following sentence pair in each runs parallel too.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the conclusion rather than the summary: keep the Kurzantwort's adjudication as the thesis statement and rewrite 8.4's opening to do forward-looking work - what the asymmetry means operationally for a holder (which of the three simultaneous conditions is most likely to break first, and what position the reader is implicitly taking by holding through the 2026-27 commission-rate window). 8.5's indicators already exist; 8.4 should set up their decision relevance rather than re-announce the verdict.
